sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The shape is not smooth: FY2023 revenue was flat at 0.2% growth [D284], then FY2024 rose 125.9% [D338], FY2025 114.2% [D393] and FY2026 65.5% [D448].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P23][P22].
FY2026 growth was again data center compute and networking, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue [D620] and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D622][D448].
Within it, Compute contributed 46.1pp and Networking 14.1pp in FY2026 [D629][D636].
Data Center networking grew 142% on the NVLink compute fabric ramp for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5% [D449][D448], an incremental margin of 57.3% [D475].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% against net income growth of 64.7% [D452][D450], with the diluted share count down 1.2% [D470].
Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026 [F50], against a window median of 32.8% [D813] and a high of 62.4% in FY2025 [D812].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1% [F30][D462], the main drag on the 2.0pp operating-margin decline [D463].
Compute & Networking operating income absorbed a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge in Q1 FY2026 [P7].
R&D fell to 8.6% of revenue from 9.9% [D427][D372], adding 1.3pp to margin [D478], while SG&A added 0.6pp [D479].
The effective tax rate rose to 15.1% [D434] on lower relative stock-compensation and research-credit benefits [P2].
Operating cash flow was $102.7 billion and free cash flow $96.7 billion in FY2026 [F100][F110], a 44.8% free-cash-flow margin [D432].
Free cash flow covered net income 0.81x in FY2026 [D436], below the 1.16x semis peer median [D847].
Capex was 2.8% of revenue [D431] but 2.13x D&A [D437], as inventory rose 112.3% [D474] and receivables 66.8% [D473].
FY2024 operating cash flow rose on revenue growth, helped by $557 million of customer payments received ahead of invoice due dates [P18].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion in FY2026 from $34.7 billion [D441][D386], just 1.0% of revenue [D442].
That still ranks in the 83rd percentile of six semis peers, whose median net cash is -13.9% of revenue [D844][D845].
Investing outflow of $52.2 billion [F120] rose on equity investment purchases and a Groq license agreement [P1].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion [D443] were 42.5% of free cash flow [D444], and the share count fell 1.2% [D470].
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue in FY2023 and fell 25.0% [D753][D754], cutting operating income 57.9% that year [D285].
The FY2023 decline reflected $2.17 billion of inventory provisions on excess Ampere Gaming and Data Center supply [P38].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026, subtracting 4.1pp from growth [D545][D546], after growing 103.1% in FY2025 [D542].
Two direct customers represented 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue [P6], a concentration risk the filings flag.
Product revenue members sum to 190% of consolidated FY2026 revenue, so segment lines must not be added [R2].
If gross margin falls below the FY2026 level of 71.1% [F30], the H20 charge would look structural rather than one-off; watch the FY2027 10-K.
If operating cash flow conversion stays below the 0.83x window median [D828], working-capital build is outpacing earnings; watch the FY2027 cash flow statement.
If China revenue falls below the FY2026 $19.7 billion [S24], the geographic mix shift toward the US at 69.3% [D503] would accelerate; watch the FY2027 disaggregation.
